clue.text: A beater for those who carry the guns?

definitions.text: A beater for those who carry the guns?

parts.words: A beater for those who carry the guns?
parts.note: reads like a shooting-party beater flushing game for the guns, but means a young soldier who beats the drum for an army of riflemen

explanation.surface: A grouse-shoot beater driving birds towards the people holding shotguns.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British shoot, beaters drive birds towards 'the guns' (the shooters); here the beater strikes a drum and the gun-carriers are infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a lad who beats the drum for a regiment of soldiers bearing rifles.

clue.text: Brief notes jazz fans raised with the censor

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: cats is old slang for jazz enthusiasts
Cato the Elder was the famous Roman censor

explanation.surface: Short messages from jazz lovers are brought up with the official who vets content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns CATS into STAC in this down light; Cato held the Roman office of censor.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, staccato means notes played short and detached from one another.

clue.text: A drink that the darts player needs

definitions.meaning: in darts, the outer ring scoring twice; a player must finish on one

explanation.definitionFit: A double is both a large spirit measure and the ring on a dartboard needed to finish a game.

clue.text: Little land is left to the East

parts.note: taken as written; the run of letters across 'is left' is a coincidence, since 'to the East' must supply the final E
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Only a small plot remains on the eastern side.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a small island, a little piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: No-hoper set out, beyond recovery

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hopeless case has been set out as past saving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks part of 'set out' as one phrase but is fodder; 'out' alone signals rearranging NOHOPERSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer on the ropes is close to defeat, so the idiom means in a hopeless position.

clue.text: Secret American resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: A hidden holiday spot in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination, but it means sort again, rearranging AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceedings held in camera take place in private, out of public view, so they are kept secret.

clue.text: Don's best port?

parts.note: reads like a university fellow's finest fortified wine, but means the chief harbour city on the River Don in Russia

explanation.surface: Which bottle of port does an Oxford academic rate highest?
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a British university teacher and port a fortified wine; the city's full name is Rostov-on-Don.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostov-on-Don is the major Russian port city standing on the River Don.

clue.text: Their quarters are combed for food

definitions.text: Their quarters are combed for food

parts.words: Their quarters are combed for food
parts.note: reads like rooms being searched for something to eat, but describes honeycomb homes from which honey is harvested

explanation.surface: Soldiers' barracks are searched thoroughly for rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combed' means searched in the surface but refers to honeycomb cells in the hive.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects live in honeycomb, the cells from which honey is taken for food.

clue.text: A portion's spread out to kill vermin

indicators.note: spreading something out scatters its pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's is read as 'is', so its S counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A share of something is distributed widely to get rid of pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodent poison is a substance laid down for killing rats and similar pests.

clue.text: A quarter past twelve and not a soul to be seen

indicators.note: past means coming after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock midday
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: At quarter past twelve the street is empty, nobody visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quarter past twelve' reads as a time, 12:15; in fact a compass quarter, E, comes after NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody at all is meant by not a soul, the phrase standing for no person whatsoever.

clue.text: Taxi runs into a horse — ghastly!

indicators.note: into signals that one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A cab crashes into a horse, a horrible accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome and dwelling on death, which is a close synonym for ghastly.

clue.text: Fire stations?

parts.note: reads like bases for firefighters, but means places in the home where a fire sits

explanation.definitionFit: A hearth is the floor of a fireplace, literally a station for a domestic fire.

clue.text: Point to eradicate or delete

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
rase is a variant spelling of raze, to wipe out completely

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove or strike something out entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or remove, the same as deleting text.

clue.text: Resolve us in another way

indicators.note: putting the letters in another way means arranging them differently

explanation.surface: A plea to work out our own problems by a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: rearranging RESOLVEUS gives a reflexive form of 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun is simply the first-person plural 'us' expressed in a different form.

clue.text: Vital accessory for high-fliers

parts.note: reads like a status symbol for successful people, but means breathing apparatus for pilots at altitude

explanation.surface: The must-have item for ambitious, successful executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-fliers' sounds like ambitious achievers; literally it is airmen at altitude, where thin air makes breathing apparatus vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots flying at great height need breathing equipment supplying air, literally vital for life.

clue.text: Foreign girls who drop in after marriage

definitions.text: Foreign girls who drop in after marriage

parts.words: Foreign girls who drop in after marriage
parts.note: reads like visitors calling once wed, but means Italian unmarried women whose title loses the letters I and N when they wed

explanation.surface: Young women from abroad who pay a visit once they are married.
explanation.walkthrough: An Italian Miss becomes Signora, Mrs, on marrying: the title literally drops 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Italian young unmarried women, addressed by the title meaning Miss.

clue.text: Generally having a regional accent?

definitions.meaning: in general terms, without going into detail
talking with a strong, broad local accent

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in general terms, and literally describes talking in a broad dialect.

clue.text: The Spanish, say, take time out to find a deputy

indicators.note: with 'out', taking a piece outside wraps it around the others
with 'take', it places this piece on the outside of the rest

parts.note: a date is a point in time
el is Spanish for 'the'
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A Spaniard, for instance, takes a break to find someone to stand in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take time out' sounds like having a rest; 'take ... out' is the container signal, putting the time word around the Spanish article and the 'say' abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is someone sent to act or speak on another's behalf, as a deputy does.

clue.text: Maintained unusual tidiness

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone kept up an unexpected neatness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintained' looks like the tidiness being kept up, but it means asserted firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to keep asserting it, which is what insisting means.

clue.text: Vocalists who scale the heights

parts.note: reads like singers hitting high notes, but means Alpine singers in the mountains

explanation.surface: Singers who climb up to the top notes of their range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' suggests a musical scale; the singers here are in the Alps, famous for warbling calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singers alternate rapidly between chest voice and falsetto, a tradition of the mountains.

clue.text: He gives his companions a hand

definitions.text: He gives his companions a hand

parts.words: He gives his companions a hand
parts.note: reads like someone helping friends, but means the card player handing out the cards

explanation.surface: A helpful man assists his friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hand' sounds like help; in card games a hand is the set of cards each player is given.
explanation.definitionFit: At cards, the person who distributes the cards gives each player at the table a hand.

clue.text: A blow to Wilde's initial enthusiasm

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blow of wind
O is the first initial of Oscar Wilde

explanation.surface: A blast of wind damped the playwright's early eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilde's initial' tempts W, the first letter of the surname; it is O, for Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means hearty relish and keen enjoyment, a synonym for enthusiasm.

clue.text: Capacity to get on after bitterness?

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the one it follows

parts.note: gall means bitterness or rancour

explanation.surface: Can someone get along after harbouring resentment?
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of volume, so the word names a measure of capacity.

clue.text: A number in Malaga out to form a union

indicators.note: in signals that one piece is placed inside the other
out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A group of people in the Spanish city leave to set up a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside MALAGA, then 'out' rearranges MAMLAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or blend, a combination of parts joined into one.

clue.text: Just open for a drink

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, especially of beer

explanation.surface: The pub is barely open for someone to have a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a jar' is everyday British slang for a glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open, open only just a little.

clue.text: Firm has deficit — one in large figures

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a loss is a financial deficit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company runs at a loss, one of the big numbers on its accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large figures' suggests big sums of money; it means huge statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are gigantic statues, plural of the word for an enormous figure like Rhodes's.

clue.text: Caught boy getting dressed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad is caught while putting his clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning wearing clothes.

clue.text: Porter right on his toes

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A hotel porter is quite rightly quick on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman; it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's toes means being watchful and ready, which is a synonym for wary.

clue.text: Flattery works with neighbours, for example

parts.note: soap is slang for flattery, as in soft soap
opera is the plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: Sweet-talking goes down well with the people next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neighbours' reads as the people next door; it is Neighbours, a long-running Australian TV serial popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbours is a long-running Australian television serial drama, an example of the genre.
